title: Masai Mara Safari Cost, Line by Line From Gate Fees to Fly-In Camps
meta_title: Masai Mara Safari Cost: Prices by Budget and Season
meta_description: Masai Mara safari cost by budget and season: reserve fees, camp rates, road vs fly-in and sample per-person budgets from our Nairobi team.
excerpt: What a Masai Mara safari cost looks like in practice: checked reserve fees, camp rate bands, road vs fly-in and sample budgets per person.
content:
The Masai Mara safari cost for most travellers falls between about US$300 and US$3,000 per person per day, depending on where you sleep, how you get there and the month you travel. Reserve fees are US$100 or US$200 per adult per day, and your choice of camp moves the total more than anything else.

Prices online swing wildly, and many quotes leave out fees, flights or tips until late in the booking. This guide breaks the Masai Mara safari cost down line by line, with checked fee figures, honest camp rate bands and sample budgets, so you can compare any quote, including our Kenya safari packages, with confidence.

Quick Facts

  • Reserve fee: US$100 per non-resident adult per day January-June, US$200 July-December (checked November 2026)
  • Children: US$50 per day for ages 9-17; age 8 and under free
  • Ticket rule: Each ticket covers 12 hours, 6am to 6pm, and does not carry overnight
  • Typical daily spend: About US$300-500 budget, US$600-1,000 mid-range, US$1,500-3,000+ luxury per person (estimates)
  • Biggest variable: Your camp, which drives most of the Masai Mara safari cost
  • Cheapest months: April to early June, when the low fee and low-season camp rates overlap

How Much Does a Mara Safari Cost Per Day?

A Mara safari costs roughly US$300-500 per person per day on a budget, US$600-1,000 mid-range and US$1,500-3,000 or more at the top end. Those daily figures include the reserve fee, a full-board bed and game drives, and they assume two people sharing a room and a vehicle.

The daily rate is the simplest way to compare a Masai Mara safari cost across offers, because a good package bundles everything: transport from Nairobi, a pop-up roof 4x4 with a driver-guide, meals and fees. Solo travellers pay more, since single supplements and a private vehicle are not shared. Families with children under nine save on fees, as young children enter free.

If you are planning a longer trip through several parks, our guide to the cost of a Kenya safari covers Amboseli, Lake Nakuru and Samburu as well. This page stays focused on the Masai Mara safari cost, where the numbers behave differently because of the seasonal reserve fee.

What Are the Masai Mara Reserve Fees?

The Masai Mara National Reserve charges non-resident adults US$100 per day from January to June and US$200 per day from July to December, children aged 9 to 17 pay US$50, and under-8s go free (checked November 2026). The Mara Triangle, run by the Mara Conservancy, applies the same structure.

Each ticket is valid for 12 hours, from 6am to 6pm, regardless of when you enter, and it does not roll over to the next morning. The Mara Triangle conservation fees page also explains that it is cashless: you pay by card or M-Pesa through the electronic ticketing system, and East African residents need ID to claim resident rates. Fees do change, so confirm the current rate before you book, as it is the one fixed line in every Masai Mara safari cost.

How the 12-hour ticket changes your Masai Mara safari cost

Because tickets end at 6pm, guests staying outside the gates pay a fresh fee every day they drive in. Camps inside the reserve avoid the daily exit, but you still pay one fee for every day you spend in the reserve. Count your fee days, not your nights: a three-night stay by road usually means three or four ticket days, depending on your arrival time and how early you leave on the last morning.

VisitorJanuary-JuneJuly-December
Non-resident adult (18+)US$100 per dayUS$200 per day
Non-resident child (9-17)US$50 per dayUS$50 per day
Child aged 8 and underFreeFree
3 fee days, one adultUS$300US$600

Private conservancies bordering the reserve, such as Mara North, Naboisho and Olare Motorogi, work differently. Their conservation fees are normally built into the camp's nightly rate and paid through the camp, which is why the Masai Mara safari cost at a conservancy camp can look high until you notice the fees are already inside the price. Our reserve vs conservancy comparison explains what you gain for that money, and the Masai Mara entrance fee guide covers resident and student rates in more detail.

Masai Mara Safari Prices Per Person by Budget

Masai Mara safari prices per person for three nights run from about US$1,000 on a budget road trip to US$9,000 or more for a peak-season luxury stay. The table below shows estimates for July to December, built from the verified reserve fees plus typical published camp rate bands.

StyleWhat you get3 nights per person (estimate)
BudgetSimple tented camp near a gate, shared or small-group vehicle, road transferUS$1,000-1,600
Mid-rangeComfortable tented camp, private 4x4 for two, road transferUS$2,300-3,300
LuxuryLodge or conservancy camp, fly-in, guided drives includedUS$5,500-9,000+

From January to June, take roughly US$300 per adult off each Masai Mara safari cost line for the lower reserve fee, and often more again because many camps cut their own rates in the April-May rains. For named camps at each level, see our Masai Mara camps by budget.

Budget camps near the gates

Budget camps sit outside the reserve, mostly around Sekenani and Talek gates, and charge roughly US$100-250 per person per night full board (estimate). Staying here trims the accommodation line of your Masai Mara safari cost, though you pay the gate fee each day you drive in, and shared vehicles mean less say over how long you stay at a sighting.

Mid-range tented camps

Mid-range tented camps charge roughly US$300-650 per person per night, with en-suite tents, hot showers and good food. Add a private vehicle and guide, usually shared between two to six people, and this is where most first-time visitors land. It buys flexibility: you decide when to leave in the morning and how long to wait at a river crossing.

What a luxury Masai Mara safari cost looks like

At the top end, prices climb fast. Angama Mara, on the Oloololo Escarpment above the Mara Triangle, lists US$1,850 per person per night in standard season and US$2,750 in peak season in its published rates on its own website (checked November 2026). That rate covers meals, most drinks, shared game drives and flights from Nairobi, but reserve fees, a private vehicle and tips are extra.

A luxury Masai Mara safari cost is easier to judge once you read what is excluded. Always ask whether a lodge rate covers reserve fees, flights and conservation levies, because two camps with the same nightly figure can end up hundreds of dollars apart over three nights.

Is It Cheaper to Drive or Fly to the Mara?

Driving from Nairobi is the cheaper way to reach the Mara, because the road transfer is usually included in a package and the vehicle is shared. Flying costs more per person but turns a five to six hour drive into a 45-75 minute hop from Wilson Airport.

Scheduled light-aircraft fares from Wilson to the Mara airstrips came out at roughly US$250-350 per person each way in recent fare searches (checked November 2026, an estimate). Bags on these flights are normally limited to soft holdalls of around 15kg, which matters if you are carrying camera gear. Flying in also trims the vehicle line of your Masai Mara safari cost, since many camps include drives for fly-in guests.

OptionTime from NairobiBest for
Road, private 4x4About 5-6 hoursCouples, families and groups watching the budget
Road, shared vehicleAbout 5-6 hoursSolo travellers and tight budgets
Scheduled flight45-75 minutesShort stays and travellers who want more time in the bush

For a group of four or more, road almost always gives the lower Masai Mara safari cost. For two people with only three nights, flying can be worth it, as you gain most of a game-drive day at each end. Our fly-in safari packages combine flights, camps and fees in one price.

When Is the Masai Mara Safari Cost Lowest?

The Masai Mara safari cost is lowest from April to early June, when the long rains bring low-season camp rates and the reserve fee is still US$100. It peaks from July to October, during the Great Migration, when both fees and camp rates hit their highest point.

MonthsReserve feePrice and wildlife
January-MarchUS$100Dry, green plains and resident predators; strong value
April-early JuneUS$100Long rains, lowest camp rates, some camps close
July-OctoberUS$200Migration herds and river crossings; highest prices, book early
November-mid DecemberUS$200Short rains, fewer vehicles, some camps discount
Late DecemberUS$200Festive peak; many camps charge peak rates

Timing the migration is a balancing act, as the herds usually arrive in July and leave by October, but the exact weeks change each year. Our best time to visit the Masai Mara guide and the Mara migration timing guide help you choose a window before you lock in dates.

Which Extras Add to the Masai Mara Cost?

The extras that most often push up the Masai Mara cost are a balloon flight, tips, drinks at budget and mid-range camps, laundry and travel insurance. Together they can add US$600-1,000 per person to a three-night trip, so build them in from the start.

A dawn balloon flight is the biggest single extra in any Masai Mara safari cost. Our trip pages list it as an option at US$480-500 per person, and published rates generally sit around US$450-600. The Masai Mara balloon safari guide explains launch sites, timings and what the bush breakfast includes.

Tips are the other line people forget. Divulge Adventures suggests about US$10 per person per day for your driver-guide, plus a modest amount for camp staff, and our tipping in Kenya guide gives fair amounts for each role. Add a Maasai village visit if it is not already in your itinerary, and keep a little spare for curios.

Hidden Masai Mara price traps to check in a quote

Ask whether a quoted Masai Mara safari cost counts fee days correctly, includes the reserve or conservancy fees, and states the vehicle type. A cheap quote using a minibus instead of a 4x4 can mean a rougher ride and less flexibility when roads turn muddy. Also check whether drinks and laundry are included, as these vary by camp.

What Does a Real Masai Mara Package Cost?

A real Masai Mara package from Nairobi starts from around US$1,600 per adult for a short road trip with park fees included. Our 4 day Naivasha, Nakuru and Masai Mara safari starts from US$1,627 per adult, with two nights in the Mara, fees, transport, meals and guiding.

That Masai Mara safari cost excludes the balloon, insurance, visas, international flights and tips, and the final figure depends on your dates, group size and lodges. If you would rather fly, the 3 day Masai Mara fly-in safari is priced on request, so we can match the camp and season to your budget.

Insider Tips

  • Count fee days: Your Masai Mara safari cost depends on days inside the reserve, not nights, so count them first
  • Travel in June: Late June still has the lower fee, and the first herds sometimes arrive early
  • Share the vehicle: A private 4x4 split four ways costs far less per person than one split two ways
  • Ask about free nights: Some camps offer stay-four-pay-three deals in standard season
  • Carry a card: Mara Triangle gates are cashless, so bring a Visa card or M-Pesa
  • Budget tips in cash: US dollars or shillings in small notes make tipping easy

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does a Masai Mara safari cost per person?

The Masai Mara safari cost for three nights is about US$1,000-1,600 per person on a budget road trip, US$2,300-3,300 mid-range and US$5,500-9,000 or more fly-in luxury. These are July-December estimates; January to June is several hundred dollars cheaper.

What are the Masai Mara prices for park entry?

Masai Mara prices for entry were US$100 per non-resident adult per day from January to June and US$200 from July to December, with children aged 9 to 17 at US$50 and under-8s free (checked November 2026). Tickets last 12 hours, from 6am to 6pm, so confirm the current rate before you book.

Is it cheaper to drive or fly to the Masai Mara?

Driving to the Masai Mara is cheaper, because road transfer is built into most package prices and a vehicle is shared by the whole group. Flying from Wilson Airport costs roughly US$250-350 per person each way in recent fare searches, but it saves about five hours on the road and a fee day you would otherwise spend travelling.

When is the Masai Mara cost lowest?

The Masai Mara cost is lowest from April to early June, when the long rains bring low-season camp rates and the reserve fee sits at US$100 instead of US$200. January to March is also good value, with dry plains, resident wildlife and lower fees, though it falls outside the migration months.

Are tips included in the Masai Mara price?

Tips are not usually included in the Masai Mara price, whether you book a lodge directly or a package. Divulge Adventures suggests about US$10 per person per day for your driver-guide, plus a little for camp staff, but tipping is a thank-you and never compulsory. Budget it in cash, in US dollars or Kenyan shillings.

Final Thoughts

Once you know the reserve fee for your month and the camp level you want, the Masai Mara safari cost stops being a mystery. Fees are fixed and camp rates sit in clear bands, so the real choice is how you trade comfort and travel time against your budget.
